stories.headline: Intellia to Report First-Ever Phase 3 In Vivo CRISPR Gene-Editing Data on Monday

key_facts.fact: Intellia Therapeutics announced it will report topline data from HAELO, the first-ever Phase 3 trial of an in vivo CRISPR gene-editing therapy, at 8:00 AM EDT on April 27
key_facts.excerpt: Intellia Therapeutics to Report Topline Data from Global Phase 3 HAELO Clinical Trial of Lonvoguran Ziclumeran in Hereditary Angioedema on April 27, 2026

key_facts.fact: Intellia shares jumped 19.3% after hours to $16.26 on April 25, following a 14.1% decline during regular trading to $13.63
key_facts.excerpt: Intellia finished Friday at $13.63, sinking 14.1%. Then, after hours, shares bounced back 19.3% to $16.26

key_facts.fact: HAELO is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with 80 participants evaluating a single 50mg infusion of lonvoguran ziclumeran for hereditary angioedema (HAE)
key_facts.excerpt: 80 participants were given either a single 50 mg lonvo-z infusion or placebo. The main measure: number of HAE attacks recorded between week 5 and week 28.

key_facts.fact: In Phase 1/2 data, 31 out of 32 patients on the 50mg dose stayed attack-free without ongoing prophylaxis, with follow-up reaching three years
key_facts.excerpt: In its earlier Phase 1/2 data, Intellia reported that 31 out of 32 patients on the 50 mg dose stayed attack-free and didn't need ongoing prophylaxis at the data cutoff.

key_facts.fact: If Phase 3 data are positive, Intellia plans a US biologics license application in H2 2026, with potential launch in H1 2027; the company holds $605.1 million in cash
key_facts.excerpt: If the data impress, company filings indicate a U.S. biologics license application could follow in the back half of 2026, teeing up a potential launch in the U.S. during the first half of 2027.

key_facts.fact: The therapy targets the KLKB1 gene in the liver to knock down kallikrein, a key protein in the swelling cascade; rivals include Ionis's Dawnzera and KalVista's Ekterly
key_facts.excerpt: Ionis secured U.S. approval in 2025 for Dawnzera, a preventive HAE therapy. Takeda's Takhzyro remains on the market. KalVista's Ekterly just made history as the first oral, on-demand treatment for acute HAE attacks to clear the FDA.

stories.headline: Musk Drops Fraud Claims Against OpenAI, Narrowing $134B Trial to Two Key Claims

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers dismissed Musk's fraud and constructive fraud claims at his own request on April 24, leaving only two of the original 26 claims: unjust enrichment and breach of charitable trust.
key_facts.excerpt: On April 24th, US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers agreed to dismiss Musk's fraud and constructive fraud claims in a bid to streamline the case. This would leave just two claims to proceed to trial of the 26 originally included in his November 2024 complaint.

key_facts.fact: Jury selection is scheduled for Monday April 27 at federal court in Oakland, California, with opening arguments to follow on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Jury selection is scheduled to begin Monday, with opening arguments to follow on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Musk alleges OpenAI deviated from its founding nonprofit mission after securing billions from Microsoft and transitioning to a for-profit structure. He contributed $38 million in seed funding in 2015.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk argues that OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit but later turned into a for-profit company with backing from Microsoft. He says he contributed $38 million in seed funding in 2015.

key_facts.fact: Musk strategically dropped fraud claims to focus jurors on whether OpenAI benefits humanity rather than serving as a 'wealth machine,' avoiding complex evidentiary hurdles around intent.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Musk, this would allow jurors to focus on his goal of ensuring that OpenAI benefits humanity rather than serving as a 'wealth machine.'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI, Altman, Brockman, and Microsoft have denied the allegations, calling the lawsuit 'part of Musk's ongoing pattern of harassment' and accusing him of trying to benefit his own AI company, xAI.
key_facts.excerpt: The company and its leaders have all denied wrongdoing, with OpenAI claiming that the lawsuit is 'part of [Musk's] ongoing pattern of harassment.' The company also said that Musk is trying to slow them down and benefit his own business, xAI.

stories.headline: Wisconsin Regulators Force Data Centers to Pay Full Energy Costs, Block Cost-Shifting to Residents

key_facts.fact: Wisconsin's Public Service Commission unanimously approved a modified special energy rate requiring data centers to pay 100% of new natural gas plant costs, rejecting We Energies' plan that would have shifted 25% to residential customers
key_facts.excerpt: The commission denied We Energies' plan to divide the cost of two new natural gas plants between data centers and existing customers. We Energies proposed that data center companies pay 75% of the plants' capital costs, while other ratepayers cover the remaining 25%.

key_facts.fact: The decision affects Microsoft's Mount Pleasant campus (~900 MW) and a $15 billion Port Washington project for OpenAI and Oracle that could use up to 3.5 GW at full build-out
key_facts.excerpt: The first two phases of Microsoft's data center campus in Mount Pleasant will need around 900 megawatts. The Port Washington project could use up to 3.5 gigawatts at full build out.

key_facts.fact: We Energies plans to spend $19.3 billion on new electricity generation over five years, aiming to double its energy generating capacity by 2030 to serve data centers
key_facts.excerpt: The company is preparing to spend $19.3 billion on new electricity generation over five years. The decision comes as data centers in Mount Pleasant and Port Washington could double We Energies' energy demand by 2030.

key_facts.fact: Regulators lowered the mandatory rate threshold from 500 MW to 100 MW and extended service agreements from 10 to 15 years to prevent cost-shifting during construction phases
key_facts.excerpt: The commission also required projects enroll in the special rate if they use at least 100 megawatts of power. The commission also lengthened data center service agreements from a proposed 10 to 15 years.

key_facts.fact: Nearly 70% of Wisconsin voters said data center costs outweigh their benefits; more than 2,000 public comments were submitted opposing the original plan
key_facts.excerpt: PSC officials said more than 2,000 public comments were submitted.

key_facts.fact: We Energies said the new rate structure could serve as a model for other states looking to meet data center needs while protecting other energy customers
key_facts.excerpt: We Energies has said the new rate could serve as a model for other states looking to meet data center needs while protecting other energy customers.

sources.title: Regulators modify, and then approve We Energies' new electric rate for data centers
State regulators change We Energies' data center rate proposal to protect customers
Wisconsin forces data centers to pay their own energy bills, and other states are watching
